cases.question: When a route becomes a back-navigation page, what must the shared Page shell do with header chrome, quick links, and the single vertical scroller?
criteria: One React tree, one page scroller, and headerQuickLinks stay in the sticky header dock.
Back replaces the menu on back-navigation pages; the page content stays inert/scroll-locked only through the shared shell contract.
No page-local main scroller or second AppHeader appears inside route content.
failureCriteria: Duplicating header chrome or rendering both back and menu.
Moving quick links out of the shared header or introducing an extra page-local scroll owner.
cases.discriminator: A cheaper model can restate the shell shape, but the current pin must reconcile route chrome, scroll ownership, and the sticky header contract across source and tests.

cases.question: How should shared Section and ResponsiveSectionGrid primitives preserve semantic structure while remaining reusable for dashboard pages?
criteria: Section must remain a semantic section with an h2 title, optional Description, and forwarded span.
ResponsiveSectionGrid must preserve DOM order and explicit span semantics instead of inventing page-local wrappers.
Shared content should be composed from the primitives rather than duplicated as ad hoc divs.
failureCriteria: Reordering children or changing heading semantics.
Replacing the shared primitives with page-local container markup.
cases.discriminator: This case forces the answer to preserve semantic reuse across two primitives, which a cheaper model often collapses into generic wrapper advice.

cases.question: What exact grid contract must centered Quick Links follow so text-aware fill behavior stays distinct from square room tiles?
criteria: Centered Quick Links uses text-aware spans and fillRows=except-last behavior, not the square-tile sizing helper.
Non-final rows can absorb spare tracks, but the final row keeps its required spans and left alignment.
Card text width must drive measured layout; equal-width forcing is only correct when the tests explicitly request it.
failureCriteria: Treating Quick Links like the square room/admin grid.
Centering or inflating the final row, or ignoring label measurement.
cases.discriminator: The cheap failure mode is to memorize the 2+2 / 2+1+1 / 2 example without preserving the label-driven measurement logic that makes the grid text-aware.

cases.question: How should ModalSheet choose between opaque backing, auto blur bands, and mounted close-state geometry?
criteria: The sheet keeps the hardcoded hass-popup treatment and uses the opaque fallback when the auto backdrop bands are unsupported or unaudited.
Closing must render open=false while the sheet stays mounted so the exit animation and geometry freeze complete.
Geometry intent and body tier stay stable across the mounted close frame instead of reflowing or remounting.
failureCriteria: Swapping to a translucent blue/glass surface or unmounting immediately on close.
Letting resize, rotation, or a custom surface silently change the closing frame.
cases.validator: npm run test:run -- src/components/core/ModalSheet.test.tsx && npm run design:check
cases.discriminator: This requires combining runtime lifecycle, CSS backing, and geometry policy; a cheaper challenger usually answers only the animation part.

cases.question: Which files are allowed to read safe-area env() values, and how should fixed shell chrome respect those insets?
criteria: Only the token file reads env(safe-area-inset-*); product CSS consumes the resolved rd-safe variables.
Fixed nav/header chrome respects the safe rectangle and keeps the back/menu contract intact.
Pointer focus chrome stays neutral on taps while keyboard focus remains intentional.
failureCriteria: Reading env() directly in product styles or hard-coding inset constants.
Letting headers, nav, or buttons leak outside the safe rectangle.
cases.discriminator: The answer has to connect tokenization, shell positioning, and focus treatment; a cheaper model typically misses the safe-area ownership rule.

cases.question: What visual feedback is allowed on dashboard tiles and toggles, and what must never persist after a tap?
criteria: No press-only visual :active feedback, opacity flash, or border flash is added.
Tap focus must not leave a persistent white outline or selected border; keyboard focus can remain explicit.
Persistent checked, disabled, unavailable, and HA-derived state indicators are still allowed.
failureCriteria: Adding touch-only press animations or leaving pointer-induced white chrome behind.
Erasing legitimate keyboard focus treatment or state-derived borders.
cases.validator: npm run design:check && npm run test:run -- src/components/core/ToggleControl.test.tsx src/components/core/GlassTile.semantics.test.tsx
cases.discriminator: The pin has to honor both visual and accessibility state; cheaper answers usually talk about one and forget the other.

cases.question: How do typed accessories decide whether a chevron appears, and which semantics stay noninteractive?
criteria: Chevron disclosure is valid only for modal or navigate semantics.
External, selection, value, and state displays use their own marker/text treatment and do not gain button semantics or tab stops.
The answer should identify that semantics are explicit typed values, not inferred from labels, icons, or legacy disclosure booleans.
failureCriteria: Using the chevron on command/toggle controls or on noninteractive state/value displays.
Inferring semantics from title text or entity domain instead of the shared discriminated union.
cases.discriminator: This case separates a true typed-semantic answer from a surface-level icon shuffle.

cases.question: How do GlassTile disclosure, toggle roles, and sibling rail controls stay isolated from one another?
criteria: Modal and navigation disclosure come only from the typed semantics resolver, not the legacy disclosure flag alone.
Toggle tiles expose switch semantics and checked state without misusing aria-pressed.
Rail controls remain sibling buttons; clicking them must not bubble into the main tile action.
failureCriteria: Treating any disclosure prop as modal disclosure.
Collapsing the rail into the main tile or losing the switch role/state contract.
cases.discriminator: The answer has to preserve event boundaries and aria state, not just render the right icon.

cases.question: How do SelectActionField and ToggleControl keep selection, command, and switch behaviors isolated?
criteria: The select remains a combobox and the adjacent action remains a separate command button.
ToggleControl keeps switch semantics, keyboard activation, and pointer-focus suppression without breaking disabled behavior.
Action disabling must be independent of the select value itself.
failureCriteria: Merging the select and command into one control or losing the keyboard path on the switch.
Letting pointer focus leave a visible border or tab stop behind on touch.
cases.discriminator: A cheaper model can describe the widgets, but the current pin must preserve the separate semantics and keyboard behavior.

cases.question: For the bathroom fan tile, which displayed states map to which HA-owned services and which controls must stay independent?
criteria: The main tile opens the modal; lock and power remain sibling toggle controls.
Lock and power call the guest_bathroom_fan_command script with distinct commands and opposite target states.
Unavailable controls disable the toggles but must not block modal access.
failureCriteria: Using one service path for both controls or collapsing them into the main tile action.
Letting an unavailable control suppress the modal opener.
cases.discriminator: This case forces explicit state-to-service mapping instead of assuming one generic action per tile.

cases.question: How does the bathroom fan modal map timer state, auto-unlock, and cancellation to HA service calls?
criteria: Timer start uses the guest_bathroom_fan_command script with timer_start and the auto_unlock flag when requested.
Clear invokes timer_cancel, and the auto-unlock checkbox toggles its own command path.
The countdown is deadline-based while active and is not running while the modal is retained closed.
failureCriteria: Folding start/cancel/auto-unlock into one service call.
Continuing the timer interval after close or missing the deadline-based countdown.
cases.discriminator: The pin has to reason about live fan state transitions and interval gating, not just button labels.

cases.question: Which todo-list actions route through todo.update_item, and when does the completion script replace it?
criteria: Default completion goes through todo.update_item with the target entity and the next status.
When completionScript is provided, completed items call that script instead of todo.update_item.
Optimistic status hiding must clear when the live entity refresh arrives, and edit actions stay separate from completion.
failureCriteria: Mixing the script and todo service paths or omitting the target/status payload.
Losing optimistic hiding or exposing task descriptions as subtitles.
cases.discriminator: This case requires preserving HA-owned side effects while also keeping the optimistic UI path intact.

cases.question: What should a shared page scaffold provide before any dashboard-specific content is added?
criteria: A Page scaffold wraps the route in the shared shell with exactly one scroller and the shared header actions.
Measure and headerQuickLinks are part of the scaffold contract, not page-local invention.
The scaffold must not introduce alternate layouts or duplicate chrome.
failureCriteria: Adding a second shell layer or a route-specific header implementation.
Skipping the measure prop or losing header quick links.
cases.discriminator: The task is not just page creation; it is preserving the shared shell contract that every page depends on.

cases.question: How should Section, Description, and ResponsiveSectionGrid be composed in a reusable content scaffold?
criteria: Section stays semantic and renders its description through the shared Description component.
ResponsiveSectionGrid preserves DOM order and explicit span semantics.
The scaffold is built from reusable primitives, not page-local wrapper variants.
failureCriteria: Replacing the shared primitives with page-specific div structures.
Losing the span contract or the description rendering path.
cases.discriminator: This distinguishes a real scaffold answer from a generic JSX wrapper answer.

cases.question: What reusable opener-row scaffold should be used for modal entry points and what must it preserve?
criteria: The opener row uses the shared SurfaceAccessory modal chevron and derives its accessible name from title/subtitle.
Disabled opener rows stay disabled and do not expose a modal disclosure affordance.
The shared modal picker pattern remains mounted long enough to run its close animation.
failureCriteria: Using a direct chevron import or losing the title/subtitle naming contract.
Unmounting the picker immediately on close.
cases.discriminator: The case forces reuse of the actual scaffold primitive instead of inventing one-off modal rows.

cases.question: If a codemod removes direct ModalDisclosureIcon usage, what DOM and behavior must stay unchanged?
criteria: No direct ModalDisclosureIcon import remains in product code; SurfaceAccessory owns the disclosure rendering.
Modal and navigation disclosure still render exactly the same accessible behavior and DOM markers.
The codemod must not change labels, roles, or disabled behavior.
failureCriteria: Changing aria names or button roles while moving the import.
Leaving a direct chevron import behind in any product component.
cases.discriminator: A cheap transform can rename imports, but the current pin has to prove the accessibility contract survives the codemod.

cases.question: How should a bulk semantics rename keep GlassTile, Card, and related interactions functionally identical?
criteria: The discriminated ControlSemantics union remains the source of truth for disclosure and action roles.
Toggle, modal, navigate, and command behavior stay unchanged after the rename.
No semantics rename is allowed to collapse the rail, lose switch state, or alter entity-action routing.
failureCriteria: Turning a pure rename into a behavior rewrite.
Breaking role/state mapping while the names still compile.
cases.discriminator: The case catches codemods that are syntactically correct but semantically drift from the typed union contract.

cases.question: What must a mechanical wrapper transform preserve when moving from ad hoc layout nodes to shared section primitives?
criteria: The transform must preserve semantic section headings, Description rendering, and explicit grid spans.
DOM order and content grouping stay the same after the mechanical rewrite.
The result should still be validated by the existing section tests.
failureCriteria: Replacing the shared primitives with untyped div wrappers.
Changing section order or moving description text out of the shared component.
cases.discriminator: This case separates a safe mechanical transform from a structural rewrite disguised as a codemod.

cases.question: What is the smallest reproduction path for ModalSheet close/reopen or resize regressions, and which evidence shows the bug is real?
criteria: The bug must be reproduced with the mounted close frame or a resize path before any fix is proposed.
The evidence should show why the sheet stays mounted with open=false and how rapid reopen or resize affects the rendered presentation.
The answer should point to the specific state or geometry transition, not just say 're-render it'.
failureCriteria: Claiming a fix without reproducing the lifecycle issue.
Solving the symptom by unmounting or skipping the close frame.
cases.discriminator: Debugging here depends on causal lifecycle reasoning; a cheaper model usually jumps straight to a patch idea.

cases.question: How do you reproduce and verify a bathroom-fan timer bug where the countdown or interval keeps running after close?
criteria: The reproduction must distinguish active runtime counting from the retained closed modal case.
The answer must identify the deadline-based countdown and the no-interval-while-closed contract.
The fix should preserve the active timer while eliminating the closed-state tick.
failureCriteria: Treating the timer as a fixed timeout instead of a live deadline display.
Forgetting the retained-closed case or masking it with a rerender hack.
cases.discriminator: The case requires reproducing the retained-modal behavior, which is easy to miss if the model only reads the timer code.

cases.question: What exactly should be reproduced when a light color wheel conflicts with swipe-to-dismiss and optimistic marker updates?
criteria: Swipes over the wheel must not trigger a color pick, while taps should pick a color and move the marker optimistically.
The marker owns the drag gesture, but the sheet must still be able to dismiss on non-marker swipes.
The answer should describe the gesture split, not just say 'debounce it'.
failureCriteria: Making every pointer move recolor the light or blocking sheet dismissal.
Removing the optimistic marker behavior and waiting for HA echoes.
cases.discriminator: This case only passes if the model can reason about gesture ownership and optimistic UI together.

cases.question: Which exact URLs and cache-busting rules must a valid Home Assistant dashboard validation cover?
criteria: The validation must cover the raw app, legacy sidebar dashboard, and embedded custom panel.
The raw app needs a cache-busting query string, and the legacy wrapper URL must be bumped after dist is copied.
The answer should not conflate the cached wrapper with the production bundle itself.
failureCriteria: Mentioning only one host or skipping the cache-busting rule.
Treating same-machine HTTP 200 as proof of remote LAN reachability.
cases.validator: Static contract review against the cited lines; no runtime launch is needed for the frozen case.
cases.discriminator: The pin has to remember the three-host deployment contract, not just the app URL.

cases.question: What runtime constraints define a valid LAN host for the current worktree?
criteria: The server must bind to 0.0.0.0, use strictPort, and start checking from 5176 upward.
The real backend must be used with VITE_HA_TOKEN blank for the client-visible host.
The answer should mention PID, shell/session id, cwd, and chosen port as required runtime facts.
failureCriteria: Using a mock-only or test-mode server.
Starting on the wrong port, killing another listener, or leaking secrets.
cases.validator: Static contract review against the cited lines; no server start is needed for the frozen case.
cases.discriminator: A cheaper model can name a port, but the pin must preserve the full LAN-hosting contract.

cases.question: How should reconnect validation distinguish a wrapper remount from a panel that keeps the same inner frame identity?
criteria: The validator must record the exact event, host/bridge version, inner-frame identity, and performance.timeOrigin.
It must distinguish client WebSocket interruption from layout rotation remount behavior.
It must not infer a panel remount from a different host or from stale source provenance.
failureCriteria: Conflating reconnect with remount or using source from a different run to explain older evidence.
Skipping the timeOrigin or bridge-version part of the evidence.
cases.validator: Static contract review against the cited lines; no reconnect experiment is needed for the frozen case.
cases.discriminator: This case needs a precise runtime-evidence distinction that cheaper challengers often flatten into one generic reconnect story.

cases.question: What is the authorization boundary for live Home Assistant work, and what must never be inferred?
criteria: Live HA work requires explicit authorization; it is not implied by a browser tab, a validation pass, or a repository inspection.
Unit tests should mock HAKit and services rather than calling live Home Assistant.
No answer may claim that live mutation is allowed by inference.
failureCriteria: Treating read-only inspection as permission to mutate live HA.
Using live HA in place of mocked tests or validation.
cases.validator: Static contract review against the cited lines; no live HA access is required or allowed for the frozen case.
cases.discriminator: This case tests whether the model respects the live-mutation boundary instead of drifting into operational advice.

cases.question: What evidence must be recorded when validating a live host or bridge reconnect, and what should not be overgeneralized?
criteria: The evidence must include the exact event, host or bridge version, inner frame identity, and performance.timeOrigin.
A client WebSocket interruption is not the same thing as a layout-driven iframe remount.
Older run behavior must not be explained using newer source provenance unless the provenance matches.
failureCriteria: Conflating reconnect, remount, and layout rotation into one event.
Omitting the timeOrigin or bridge-version fields.
cases.validator: Static contract review against the cited lines; no live reconnect is required for the frozen case.
cases.discriminator: The case forces the model to preserve provenance and runtime identity instead of making a vague reconnect claim.

cases.question: How must the camera/WebRTC surface interact with live audio state and mute actions?
criteria: React must dispatch and listen for the documented WebRTC mute/screenshot/audio events instead of shadow-clicking the internal volume control.
The card owns camera audio state, and the React layer should not create a separate mute source of truth.
The WebRTC element must be configured with the live HA connection and stream entity contract.
failureCriteria: Shadow-clicking the card internals or maintaining a separate body-class mute state.
Ignoring the documented live event bridge between the React shell and the custom camera card.
cases.validator: Static contract review against the cited lines; no live camera stream is required for the frozen case.
cases.discriminator: This case requires the model to reason about a live runtime bridge, not just a static component tree.

cases.question: What is the status of the experimental version 3 release machine?
criteria: The experimental release machine is disabled and cannot execute.
Its Git, Playwright, merged-build, deployment, production-verification, rollback, and cleanup drivers are not implemented.
The machine must remain disabled until those registered drivers are implemented and fault-tested.
failureCriteria: Enabling the experimental machine while it references disabled tools.
Treating the experimental machine as complete because its step graph exists.
cases.validator: Static review against the experimental machine and registered tool contracts.
cases.discriminator: The case distinguishes a specified release graph from an executable, fault-tested release implementation.

cases.question: What must be true before the deterministic release machine can be enabled and execute?
criteria: Every GitHub, build, deploy, verification, rollback, and cleanup driver must be implemented and fake-driver fault-tested.
A separate operator authorization must bind the exact release plan, tool contracts, revision, scope, side-effect class, and tool IDs.
Only registered deterministic drivers may perform GitHub, build, deployment, verification, rollback, and cleanup operations.
failureCriteria: Allowing the medium reviewer or skill text to substitute for a disabled driver.
Authorizing tool IDs without binding the current plan and complete tool contracts.
cases.validator: Static review against the version 3 experimental release-machine contracts; the machine remains disabled.
cases.discriminator: The case requires separating semantic review, operator authorization, and deterministic execution.

cases.question: What evidence may complete a future release pipeline, and when may max/long review run?
criteria: Completion requires an enabled machine, accepted terminal state, exact release-plan hash, and verified final receipt-chain hash.
Production verification must still cover the raw app, legacy wrapper, custom panel, and required responsive matrix without actuating devices.
Max/long review may run only for an evidence-bound ha-release-rollback-or-host-conflict trigger.
failureCriteria: Claiming completion from model prose or caller-supplied hashes without verifying the release machine chain.
Invoking critical review routinely or omitting host and responsive evidence.
cases.validator: Static review against the release receipt, trigger, and dashboard validation contracts; no production release is permitted.
cases.discriminator: The case combines deterministic terminal evidence, risk-triggered review, host parity, and responsive verification.
